title: Car Fleet
statement: Cars start at distinct positions on a one-lane road toward a target. A car cannot pass the car in front, so it adopts that car's speed and they become a fleet. Return the number of fleets that arrive at the target. position[i] and speed[i] describe car i.
hints: Time to arrive, if alone, is (target - position) / speed.
Sort cars by position descending, closest to the target first.
A car joins the fleet ahead when its arrival time is less than or equal to that fleet's time. Otherwise it opens a new fleet.

approaches.name: Sort and monotone times
approaches.explanation: A stack of fleet arrival times.

editorial: Sort by starting position from the target backward. The first car is a fleet. Each later car merges into the fleet ahead when it would arrive no later than that fleet, because the one-lane rule prevents passing. Otherwise its own arrival time becomes a new fleet. The number of fleets is the number of times the arrival time strictly increases as you move away from the target.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def car_fleet(target: int, position: list[int], speed: list[int]) -> int:
    cars = sorted(zip(position, speed), reverse=True)
    fleets = 0
    latest = 0.0
    for pos, spd in cars:
        time = (target - pos) / spd
        if time > latest:
            fleets += 1
            latest = time
    return fleets
